html:
Portuguese Guinea was a Portuguese colony on the coast of West Africa, between Senegal and Guinea, that became independent in 1974 as Guinea-Bissau. The map shows it from 1650 to 1914.

Portuguese sailors reached these rivers in the 1440s. Traders from the Cape Verde islands, based at Cidade Velha, settled at Cacheu, founded in 1588, and later at Bissau. For three centuries the colony was little more than these river ports, where Portuguese and African-Portuguese merchants bought enslaved people from the kingdom of Kaabu and other neighbours for the Atlantic slave trade.

The colony was run from Cape Verde until 1879. Portugal conquered the interior only in the early 1900s, against fierce resistance. In 1956 Amílcar Cabral founded the PAIGC, which fought a guerrilla war from 1963 and held most of the countryside by the early 1970s. Cabral was killed in 1973, months before the party declared independence. Portugal recognised it in 1974 after the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon, which the colonial wars had helped bring about.
sum: Portuguese Guinea was a Portuguese colony on the coast of West Africa, between Senegal and Guinea, that became independent in 1974 as Guinea-Bissau. The map shows it from 1650 to 1914.
